item.text: The query object has more quirks than standard `URLSearchParams`: it preserves empty segments inside the query string, treats `?x` as a key without `=`, and normalizes invalid `%` escapes on output. I’m coding a small serializer around those rules rather than leaning on WHATWG URL behavior.

I’ve confirmed the query codec is effectively “form encoding with tolerant UTF-8 decode”: valid `%xx` sequences decode as UTF-8, spaces become `+`, and broken bytes become replacement characters before re-encoding. I’m implementing that codec directly so malformed input round-trips the same way the executable does.

item.text: I’m doing a final black-box comparison pass. For the parser cases I’m normalizing only the program name (`test6_executable` vs `test6.mjs`); everything else still has to match byte-for-byte.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "bash -lc '
set -u
compare_case() {
  local name=\""'$1"
  shift
  local exe_out node_out exe_status node_status normalized_exe
  exe_out=$("/workspace/dataset/test6_executable" "$@" 2>&1)
  exe_status=$?
  node_out=$(node /output/test6.mjs "$@" 2>&1)
  node_status=$?
  normalized_exe=${exe_out//test6_executable/test6.mjs}
  if [ "$exe_status" -ne "$node_status" ] || [ "$normalized_exe" != "$node_out" ]; then
    printf "FAIL %s'"\\n\" \""'$name"
    printf "exe status: %s'"\\n\" \""'$exe_status"
    printf "node status: %s'"\\n\" \""'$node_status"
    printf "exe output:'"\\n%s\\n\" \""'$normalized_exe"
    printf "node output:'"\\n%s\\n\" \""'$node_out"
    return 1
  fi
  printf "PASS %s'"\\n\" \""'$name"
}
